items_missed: 1_set_agenda: Never asked for or used the customer's name, never asked 'how are you today,' never explicitly confirmed truck/crew availability for the move date (especially relevant given the fluid late-August timing tied to the renters' lease), no agenda statement, no explicit 'sound good?' confirmation.
2_probe: Never asked about stairs/floors at either address, never asked about narrow hallways/tight turns, never asked about elevator/parking/HOA access concerns.

3_pricing: No mention of disassembly/reassembly being included even though the customer was planning to break down furniture themselves, skipped No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, and On-Time Guarantee entirely, and never gave the full no-hidden-fees pitch (no credit card fee, no fuel surcharge, no assembly fees).
4_clock: Never explained the clock starts on-site when the contract opens, and no sense-check ('does that make sense?') after laying out the pricing structure.

5_estimate: Didn't address stairs/elevator or walk distance as variables, no equivalents used to help the customer visualize the job size, and no mention of assembly/disassembly as a variable despite furniture needing breakdown.
6_save_your_ass: Entire section skipped — no prep-before-move-day pitch, no consolidation examples, no carload tip, no sense-check.

7_quote_booking: No attempt to lock the move onto the schedule, 'no deposit required' never mentioned, didn't describe a bolded confirmation list or ask the customer to reply with corrections, never asked 'any other questions before I let you go,' and never gave office hours or how to reach the branch.
8_politeness: Never learned or used the customer's name at all (0 of the 3+ target), and the sign-off was a single 'Yeah' after the customer thanked him and said goodbye — no warm farewell.

9_bonus: No rapport-building or humor moments, and no insurance explanation (No Worries + 60c/lb baseline) despite it being one of the strongest things to lean on right when a customer starts comparing prices.
top_strength: Sergio handled real ambiguity well — when the customer described an uncertain move-out date tied to renters and a lease deadline, he proactively proposed a concrete two-day plan ("we would split up in the two days when we load up first day drive, stay overnight in San Antonio, then unload the next morning") and gave both a two-truck and one-truck price so the customer had "both prices there just to set a budget" while the details were still unsettled.
coaching_note: You lost this one on price with zero pushback — when the customer said your number was higher than another quote, that was the moment to explain what's actually included (No Worries damage coverage, no hidden fees, the on-time guarantee), not let the call end on 'appreciate you, bye-bye.' You also never got his name, which made the whole call feel transactional from the first line — ask for it in the first thirty seconds and use it a few times. Build the Save Your Ass prep speech and the full differentiator list into every quote, especially longer-distance moves like this one where a flat-rate competitor can undercut you on the surface and you need the value pitch to justify the price.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and thorough walking through pricing and the two-day logistics plan, but transactional throughout — never learned or used the caller's name and offered no affirmations or empathy language even when the caller described a stressful lease-overlap situation.
